subject: rat patrol
title: What If a Whole Province Had No Rats? Alberta Has Kept Them Out Since 1950

scenes.text: What if you could keep an entire province rat-free? Alberta has, for 75 years, with a patrol.
Rats reached Alberta in 1950 from Saskatchewan. By 1955 there were 573 infestations. The province declared war.
It drew a control zone 600 kilometres long and 29 wide along the border. Every farm inside is inspected at least once a year.
In the 1950s, 63 tonnes of arsenic powder went onto 8,000 buildings. Keeping a pet rat became illegal, with fines up to 5,000 dollars.
Infestations fell to between one and five a year. Hundreds of sightings still come in. Most turn out to be muskrats or mice.
Alberta is now the largest inhabited rat-free area on Earth. The rats never stopped trying. Single ones still hitch rides on trucks.

description:
What if a whole province kept rats out? Alberta, Canada, has done it since 1950 with a control zone 600 kilometres long and 29 kilometres wide along the Saskatchewan border.
Infestations went from one in 1950 to 573 in 1955, then fell to one to five a year after poison campaigns and annual inspections of every premises in the zone. Keeping a pet rat is illegal, with fines up to 5,000 dollars, and Alberta is described as the largest inhabited rat-free area in the world.
